subject: Cooking
title: Spherification: The Technique That Changed Everything
description: A fast breakdown of Spherification: The Technique That Changed Everything for builders.

hook.text: Drop liquid into a calcium bath and it forms a perfect sphere — liquid inside, gel membrane outside. Edible caviar.

buildup.text: Spherification uses sodium alginate (from seaweed) and calcium chloride to gel liquid surfaces instantly.

discovery.text: Adrià popularized it at elBulli — creating olive oil caviar, melon spheres, and cocktails that burst in your mouth.

twist.text: The technique was actually patented in 1942 by Unilever for processed foods — Adrià just made it artistic.

climax.text: Today, spherification is used in restaurants, bars, and even home kitchens — kits sell for under $20.

punchline.text: A food factory technique became the most iconic innovation in modern cooking.

quiz.question: What two chemicals are used in basic spherification?

details.summary: Spherification uses sodium alginate and calcium chloride to create liquid-filled spheres that burst with flavor in the mouth. Invented at elBulli, the technique transformed everything from olive oil into caviar-like pearls and demonstrated that food could have forms nature never intended.
details.whyItMatters: Spherification became the signature technique of molecular gastronomy and made culinary innovation visible to the public. It proved that chemistry could create entirely new eating experiences beyond traditional cooking methods.
takeaways: Sodium alginate and calcium chloride create a gel membrane around liquid
Ferran Adrià popularized the technique starting around 2003
Basic and reverse spherification produce different textures and shelf lives

faq.question: How does spherification work chemically?
faq.answer: Sodium alginate dissolved in a flavored liquid forms a gel membrane on contact with calcium chloride solution. The calcium ions cross-link alginate molecules into a thin skin while the interior stays liquid.

faq.question: Can home cooks do spherification?
faq.answer: Yes. Spherification kits with food-grade sodium alginate and calcium chloride are widely available. Basic spherification requires only mixing, dipping, and rinsing. The technique works well for juices, cocktails, and flavored oils.
